answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation expensive and slow to earn: an agent must complete verified, useful work over time before it can transact at scale, so spinning up thousands of fake identities gains nothing. Like a raven that must return to the same summit again and again before it is trusted to carry a message, and like sable fur that cannot be faked cheaply, a costly, time-bound history makes a Sybil swarm uneconomical while honest newcomers can still start small and grow.
